If Marazion Surgery in west Cornwall closed, where would its registered
residents go? This guide answers that question with the allocation model
fitted in [Where do residents register?](allocation-workflow.html). You will
hold the fitted values, close one practice, and compare the modeled practice
lists before and after: which practices gain, how many residents go outside
mainland Cornwall, and which areas move. The data are the bundled small areas,
practices, registrations and travel times described in [The Cornwall GP
example data](cornwall-data.html). The `spax()` interface and the allocation
model are experimental and may change in later versions.

The guide uses spax, with sf, dplyr and ggplot2 for tables and maps.

```{r packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(spax)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## The idea

A scenario changes the inputs and runs the model again at the same parameter
values. Nothing is refitted. In the model, each practice attracts the
residents of a small area in proportion to its supply, here its GP full-time
equivalents (FTE), discounted by travel time with the travel scale σ, in
minutes. The outside option, registering with a practice outside mainland
Cornwall, competes with all practices through the outside weight v0. A
practice with zero GP FTE attracts no one, so closing it shares its residents
among the other practices and the outside option, at the same σ and v0.

## Fit the model once

The recipe builds demand by small area (registered residents), supply by
practice (GP FTE excluding GPs in training), the travel times and the observed
registrations, and `spax()` fits the model. Demand counts every resident
registered with any practice in England, so each area's count outside mainland
Cornwall is known, and `outside = "known"` declares it. This is the fit of
[When outside counts are
known](allocation-workflow.html#when-outside-counts-are-known), which explains
its output.

```{r fit, message = FALSE}
areas <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
gp <- cornwall_gp |>
  filter(!scilly) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]
demand <- setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa)
supply <- setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)
d <- prep_data(demand, supply, travel, metadata = list(
  demand_units = "registered residents", demand_period = "July 2026",
  supply_units = "GP FTE excluding GPs in training", supply_period = "June 2026",
  travel_units = "minutes"))
flows <- obs_flows(cornwall_flows, origin = "lsoa", facility = "practice", count = "patients")

# The same registrations, with each area's outside count known
flows_known <- obs_flows(
  cornwall_flows,
  origin = "lsoa",
  facility = "practice",
  count = "patients",
  outside = "known"
)
clm_known <- spax(d, spec_clm(), observed = flows_known)
coef(clm_known)
```

The travel scale σ is about `r round(coef(clm_known)[["sigma"]], 2)` minutes and the
outside weight v0 about `r signif(coef(clm_known)[["v0"]], 2)`. These are the values
the scenarios below hold.

## Hold the fitted values

A specification with a number in every slot has nothing to fit. Here the decay
holds the fitted σ and `outside` holds the fitted v0, and `spax()` with no
observations evaluates the model at those values.

```{r hold}
spec_at <- spec_clm(
  decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = coef(clm_known)[["sigma"]]),
  outside = coef(clm_known)[["v0"]]
)
spec_at

base <- spax(d, spec_at)
```

Where `spec_clm()` alone would say `fit`, the print shows numbers, so there is
nothing left to estimate. At the fitted values the model gives each practice
the same modeled list as the fit:

```{r same-lists}
all.equal(
  as.data.frame(base, type = "facilities")$utilization,
  as.data.frame(clm_known, type = "facilities")$utilization
)
```

## Close the practice

`replace()` sets the GP FTE of Marazion Surgery (practice code L82047) to zero,
and `prep_data()` prepares the changed inputs. The practice stays in the data
with no attraction, and `spax()` evaluates the same specification.

```{r close}
closed <- spax(prep_data(demand, replace(supply, "L82047", 0), travel), spec_at)
```

The `"facilities"` table of each result holds each practice's modeled list
(`utilization`). The table below sets the two side by side and lists the
largest changes.

```{r changes}
before <- as.data.frame(base, type = "facilities")
after <- as.data.frame(closed, type = "facilities")

# Practice names, from capitals to title case
practice_name <- function(id) {
  tools::toTitleCase(tolower(gp$name[match(id, gp$practice)]))
}

changes <- data.frame(
  practice = before$facility_id,
  name = practice_name(before$facility_id),
  before = round(before$utilization),
  after = round(after$utilization)
) |>
  mutate(change = after - before)

changes |>
  arrange(desc(abs(change))) |>
  head(7)
```

```{r change-values, include = FALSE}
gain <- setNames(changes$change, changes$practice)
lost <- -gain[["L82047"]]
fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")
```

Marazion Surgery's `r fmt(lost)` modeled registrations move mostly to
nearby practices in Hayle and Penzance: Bodriggy Health Centre
(+`r fmt(gain[["L82036"]])`), Atlantic Medical Group
(+`r fmt(gain[["L82038"]])`) and Rosmellyn Surgery (+`r fmt(gain[["Y01050"]])`).
Practices farther away, such as Helston Medical Centre, gain less.

## Registrations outside mainland Cornwall

The `"origins"` table gives each small area's outside share. Multiplying each
area's outside share by its demand and summing over areas gives the number of
residents the model sends outside mainland Cornwall.

```{r outside}
outside_count <- function(result) {
  by_area <- as.data.frame(result, type = "origins")
  sum(by_area$demand * by_area$outside_share)
}

round(c(before = outside_count(base), after = outside_count(closed)))
```

```{r outside-values, include = FALSE}
outside_change <- outside_count(closed) - outside_count(base)
```

Only `r round(outside_change)` of the `r fmt(lost)` residents go outside
mainland Cornwall, because Marazion Surgery has near neighbors.

## Who moves, and where to

`predict()` gives each area's modeled share of residents at each practice
(`"allocation"`). The map shows each area's share at Marazion Surgery before
the closure, and the practices that gain more than 10 modeled registrations.

```{r scenario-map, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Map of small areas in west Cornwall shaded by the modeled share of their residents registered at Marazion Surgery, highest around Marazion between Penzance and Helston; the closed practice is marked with a red cross, and orange circles sized by the modeled registrations gained mark the receiving practices, the largest in Penzance and Hayle."}
# Each area's modeled share of residents at the closed practice
shares <- predict(base, travel, outputs = "allocation")
moved <- data.frame(
  lsoa = shares$origin_ids,
  share = shares$outputs$allocation[, "L82047"]
)
moved_map <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  select(lsoa) |>
  inner_join(moved, by = "lsoa")

# Practices that gain more than 10 modeled registrations, with locations
gained <- cornwall_gp |>
  select(practice) |>
  inner_join(
    changes |>
      filter(change > 10) |>
      select(practice, change),
    by = "practice"
  )
# Practices on one site share a point: add their gains
site <- st_coordinates(gained)
gained <- gained |>
  mutate(x = site[, 1], y = site[, 2]) |>
  group_by(x, y) |>
  summarise(change = sum(change), .groups = "drop")

# Map window over west Cornwall, in British National Grid meters
west <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = 130000, ymin = 18000, xmax = 185000, ymax = 48000),
  crs = st_crs(cornwall_lsoa)
)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = moved_map,
    aes(fill = 100 * share),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.05
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = st_union(moved_map), fill = NA, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = gained, aes(size = change), shape = 21, fill = "orange") +
  geom_sf(
    data = filter(cornwall_gp, practice == "L82047"),
    shape = 4,
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.5,
    color = "firebrick"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako",
    direction = -1,
    name = "Residents at the\nclosed practice (%)"
  ) +
  scale_size_area(name = "Modeled\nregistrations\ngained") +
  coord_sf(xlim = west[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = west[c("ymin", "ymax")]) +
  labs(
    title = "Closing Marazion Surgery (red cross): who moves and where to",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Modeled share of residents at the practice before the closure;",
      "circles are receiving practices",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

The residents who move live in the areas around Marazion, and the model sends
them mostly to the practices a short drive away. Atlantic Medical Group,
Rosmellyn Surgery and Sunnyside Surgery share one site in Penzance, so the map
shows one circle for their combined gain of
`r fmt(sum(gain[c("L82038", "Y01050", "L82070")]))`. The changes follow from
the model at fixed values of σ and v0, in which travel time and GP FTE are all
that matter. They are a model-based comparison, not an estimate of what a real
closure would cause. [Reading results](reading-results.html) says more.

## A practice without near neighbors

Closing a practice with no near neighbor sends far more residents to the
outside option. Launceston Medical Centre (L82030), on the Devon border, is an
example. The code closes it instead of Marazion Surgery and counts the
residents of its modeled list who go outside.

```{r launceston}
closed_launceston <- spax(
  prep_data(demand, replace(supply, "L82030", 0), travel),
  spec_at
)

# Residents of its modeled list who go outside, and the list itself
round(c(
  outside = outside_count(closed_launceston) - outside_count(base),
  list = before$utilization[before$facility_id == "L82030"]
))
```

```{r launceston-values, include = FALSE}
launceston_share <- (outside_count(closed_launceston) - outside_count(base)) /
  before$utilization[before$facility_id == "L82030"]
# Modeled residents at Launceston by area, and each area's nearest other practice
at_launceston <- shares$outputs$allocation[, "L82030"] * demand[shares$origin_ids]
nearest_other <- apply(travel[shares$origin_ids, colnames(travel) != "L82030"], 1, min)
far_share <- sum(at_launceston[nearest_other >= 15]) / sum(at_launceston)
keep15 <- exp(-15^2 / (2 * coef(clm_known)[["sigma"]]^2))
```

About `r round(100 * launceston_share)`% of Launceston Medical Centre's
modeled list goes to the outside option. With σ about
`r round(coef(clm_known)[["sigma"]], 1)` minutes, a practice 15 minutes away keeps
only `r signif(100 * keep15, 1)`% of the pull it would have next door. For
`r round(100 * far_share)`% of Launceston's modeled list, the nearest other
mainland practice is at least that far, so the outside option, the same in
every area, wins there.

## A smaller change: 20% more GP FTE

The same route evaluates any change in supply. Here Marazion Surgery gains 20%
more GP FTE instead of closing.

```{r larger}
larger <- spax(
  prep_data(demand, replace(supply, "L82047", 1.2 * supply[["L82047"]]), travel),
  spec_at
)

changes_larger <- data.frame(
  practice = before$facility_id,
  name = practice_name(before$facility_id),
  before = round(before$utilization),
  after = round(as.data.frame(larger, type = "facilities")$utilization)
) |>
  mutate(change = after - before)

changes_larger |>
  arrange(desc(abs(change))) |>
  head(5)
```

```{r larger-values, include = FALSE}
larger_gain <- changes_larger$change[changes_larger$practice == "L82047"]
larger_before <- changes_larger$before[changes_larger$practice == "L82047"]
```

Marazion Surgery's modeled list grows by `r fmt(larger_gain)`, or
`r round(100 * larger_gain / larger_before)`%, taken from the same neighbors
that would gain from its closure. The list grows by less than 20%, because in
the areas where the practice already draws most residents a stronger pull has
few residents left to win.
